clue.text: Having inexhaustible energy les tries exercising

indicators.note: exercising puts the letters of les and tries through their paces, working them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with boundless energy keeps at their rugby practice, trying again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercising' rearranges LESTRIES, the letters of 'les tries', into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never tires has an inexhaustible store of energy.

clue.text: Quite a knotty part of 3

indicators.note: part of says the answer sits as a run of letters inside the words quite a knotty

explanation.surface: A gnarled, knotty section of a felled tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 3 points to TIMBER, the answer at 3-down; 'part of' takes the letters running across 'quiTE A Knotty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Teak is a hard tropical wood, one kind of timber.

clue.text: Fell cry

parts.note: the shout given as a tree is cut down and about to fall, warning those nearby

explanation.definitionFit: Lumberjacks call out this word to warn that a felled tree is coming down.

clue.text: Reported restriction on country, one in Asia

indicators.note: reported says the words before are spoken, and the answer is what is heard

parts.note: a tie is a restriction, and land is a country, giving tie land

explanation.surface: News of sanctions being placed on an Asian nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' means we say TIE LAND (a restriction on a country) out loud, and it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thailand is a nation of South-East Asia, one country among many there.

clue.text: Three-sided attempt, say, sharply defined

indicators.note: say signals that the attempt word is spoken, giving a sound that is spelt differently

parts.note: an attempt is a try
angular means having sharp corners or clear-cut outlines

explanation.surface: A three-pointed design attempt with crisp edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells us TRY is only spoken: it sounds like TRI-, the prefix for three.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle has three sides, so a triangular shape is three-sided.

clue.text: Leading before second half of week, one in Kansas

parts.note: leading means being at the top

indicators.note: second half of keeps only the final two letters of the four-letter word week

parts.note: one gives A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A team topping the table late in the week, somewhere in Kansas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is the charade's order. The definition stretch is short: the answer is a city in Kansas, the state capital, with 'one' already spent on the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Topeka is the capital city of the US state of Kansas.

clue.text: Being with Timothy east for all one's days

parts.note: being means existence, that is life
Tim is the short form of the name Timothy

explanation.surface: Spending a life with Timothy out in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifetime is the whole span of one's existence, every day lived.

clue.text: Coarse soil at bottom of bay

parts.note: soil is earth

indicators.note: at bottom of picks the last letter of bay, which ends this down entry

explanation.surface: Rough, gritty soil lying at the foot of a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the last letter is at the bottom: 'at bottom of' adds Y, the end of 'bay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is crude and unrefined, so earthy can mean coarse.

clue.text: Would one dread seeing this film?

definitions.text: Would one dread seeing this film?

parts.words: Would one dread seeing this film?
parts.note: a genre of cinema designed to frighten, whose very name is a word for dread

explanation.definitionFit: The film genre is named after the terror it sets out to provoke.

clue.text: Staffordshire emblem?

parts.note: a vegetable that is a national emblem of Wales, but also the name of a market town in Staffordshire

explanation.walkthrough: The leek is Wales's emblem; Staffordshire, an English county, has a town called Leek, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable is the Welsh national emblem and shares its name with a Staffordshire town.

clue.text: Obstacles in the way of a rotter protected by rails

annotationWithheld.why: 'Obstacles in the way of a rotter protected by rails' (10): A CAD (a rotter) inside a word for rails should give BARRICADES, but no word for rails leaves BARRI...ES around it, and 'in the way' has no clear job; clue looks garbled
annotationWithheld.clue: Obstacles in the way of a rotter protected by rails

clue.text: Landlord had smaller amount alternatively

parts.note: less means a smaller amount
or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A landlord who had less money, or something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessor grants a lease, so is the landlord of the property let.

clue.text: South African boy had best part of the dressing

parts.note: a boy is a lad
the cream is the best part of anything, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: A South African lad helped himself to the best of the dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad cream is a tangy, mayonnaise-like dressing poured over salads.

clue.text: Dicky, eager, had this worn on top

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or out of order, so the letters of eager and had are jumbled

explanation.surface: An eager man in a dickey bow had something perched on his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name or a shirt-front; it is the British word for unsound, signalling the anagram of EAGERHAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Hats, helmets and caps are all items worn on the head.

clue.text: Bespatter a little soda-water

explanation.definitionFit: To spatter liquid about is to splash it, and a small dash of soda in a drink is also called a splash.

clue.text: Man accepting one ideology of devilish disposition

indicators.note: accepting means the man's name takes another piece inside itself

parts.note: Stan is a man's name, short for Stanley
one gives A, the indefinite article
an ism is any doctrine or ideology

explanation.surface: A man embracing a single creed with a wicked turn of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' builds SATAN, the devil, which suits the surface's devilish note.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship of the devil reflects a fiendish outlook, a diabolical bent of mind.

clue.text: Notice about theologian, the Parisian who was muddled

indicators.note: about means the notice word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
le is the French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A notice about a divine and a Frenchman who was confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the notice the outer piece; 'who was' merely links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An addled mind is confused and befuddled.

clue.text: Light fantasy

parts.note: a gentle, idle fantasy indulged in by day, while awake; light is also daylight, and a fantasy a dream

explanation.definitionFit: A reverie while awake is a light, idle fantasy of the waking hours.

clue.text: Trite statement about rust I'm removing

indicators.note: about means the letters of rust I'm are turned round and rearranged

explanation.surface: Platitudes about rust from someone stripping it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges RUSTIM, the letters of 'rust I'm'; 'removing' fits the picture and joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A truism is a self-evident, hackneyed remark, a platitude.

clue.text: Guide heavyweight leading performer

parts.note: a heavy weight carried is a load
the star is the leading performer in a show

explanation.surface: A hefty headline act serves as a mentor.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestar is a star used to steer by, hence anything that serves as a guiding principle.

clue.text: Order a quantity of money from beastly container!

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: Ordering a sum of cash taken from an animal's money box.
explanation.walkthrough: OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour. 'Beastly' here means of a beast, not nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The omasum is the third stomach of a ruminant such as a cow, a chamber within an animal.

clue.text: Victim coming from Cromarty relieved

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sufferer arrives from Cromarty, glad to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromarty is a small town in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr is one who suffers or dies for a cause, a sacrificial sufferer.

clue.text: Monday's theory?

parts.note: read whimsically, the first day's abbreviation plus a word for doctrine: a philosophy holding that all is one substance

explanation.definitionFit: Monism is the philosophical doctrine that reality is a single substance.

clue.text: Concerning an author's shield?

parts.note: an adjective relating to a writer named Lawrence, which also names the great Canadian rock shield

explanation.walkthrough: The Laurentian Shield is the ancient rock core of Canada; the adjective also relates to D. H. Lawrence.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to Lawrence, the novelist, and names Canada's vast Precambrian shield.

clue.text: Felix sounds pleased to do this

definitions.text: Felix sounds pleased to do this

parts.words: Felix sounds pleased to do this
parts.note: Felix is a cartoon cat, and a contented cat makes a low vibrating noise

explanation.definitionFit: A contented cat makes a soft rumbling hum in its throat.

clue.text: Prize fruit

explanation.definitionFit: A plum job is a choice reward worth winning, and the plum is also a stone fruit.

clue.text: Distances on the moon al's run round

indicators.note: round means the letters of al's run are spun around into a new order

explanation.surface: Al jogs a circuit measuring how far he gets on the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges ALSRUN; lunars are navigators' measurements of the moon's angular distance from a star.
explanation.definitionFit: In old navigation, lunar distances were angles between the moon and a star, used to find longitude.

clue.text: Powerfully-built cur mauls stranger

indicators.note: stranger means more strange, so the letters of cur mauls are made odd and rearranged

explanation.surface: A brawny dog savages a passing stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a noun for the victim; it is the comparative of strange, rearranging CURMAULS.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscular person is brawny and strongly built.
